articles.title: My background AI processes worked great in the demo and then fell apart the second they had to wait
articles.excerpt: I’ve watched this happen a bunch of times. The demo is clean: webhook hits n8n GPT-5 generates a summary Claude Opus cleans it up result gets posted to Discord or written into Airtable everybody says…
articles.body: I’ve watched this happen a bunch of times. The demo is clean: webhook hits n8n GPT-5 generates a summary Claude Opus cleans it up result gets posted to Discord or written into Airtable everybody says “nice, ship it” Then someone adds one very normal requirement: wait for approval retry if HubSpot is down pause until the customer replies resume tomorrow morning if Stripe finally sends the webhook That’s the moment your “AI workflow” stops being a sequence of API calls and starts becoming distributed systems work. And a lot of AI automation demos completely hide that fact. If your workflow can outlive one HTTP request, you need to design for background execution on purpose. The first lie your automation tells you Your first successful automation teaches the wrong lesson.

articles.title: How to Build a Secure Authentication System
articles.excerpt: Authentication is one of the most important security components of a modern software application. Websites, mobile applications, online stores, banking platforms, learning portals, and business applic…
articles.body: Authentication is one of the most important security components of a modern software application. Websites, mobile applications, online stores, banking platforms, learning portals, and business applications all need a reliable way to identify users and control access to their accounts. A basic login form may appear simple, but building a secure authentication system requires much more than accepting a username and password. A properly designed system must protect passwords, validate user input, manage sessions securely, prevent unauthorized access, handle failed login attempts, protect sensitive information, and provide a safe account recovery process.

articles.title: Why a Coding Agent Needs an MCP for Allure TestOps When a Human Can Just Open the Browser
articles.excerpt: Developers on our team switched to working through coding agents fairly quickly. In my experience, development speed grew several times over, because a large share of routine work with code moved to a…
articles.body: Developers on our team switched to working through coding agents fairly quickly. In my experience, development speed grew several times over, because a large share of routine work with code moved to agents. The processes around the code did not automatically get faster. Testing is where it became visible. My QA colleague was heavily loaded, and I asked her a simple question: how can I help? That question eventually became a small MCP server for Allure TestOps . The obvious objection: why give an agent an MCP for TestOps if a human can just open it in a browser? Because the browser was never the problem. The problem was that the developer already works through an agent, while a human still manually carries information between code, the TMS, and other tools.

articles.body: ➡️ INTRODUCTION Have you ever contacted customer support, explained your problem, and then had to explain the same thing again when you contacted them later? That is one of the common problems with traditional customer-support systems. A customer may have already reported a billing issue, requested a refund, or discussed a previous problem. But when they start a new conversation, that context may not be available. For our hackathon project, we built a Customer Support Memory Agent that uses persistent memory to remember important customer interactions and use them in future conversations.

articles.title: I Removed an API Field. Hindsight Found Who Still Needed It.
articles.excerpt: API compatibility problems are rarely difficult because removing a field is technically hard. The difficult part is knowing who still depends on that field. The result is a system with a clear separat…
articles.body: API compatibility problems are rarely difficult because removing a field is technically hard. The difficult part is knowing who still depends on that field. I started with a simple question: if I remove phone from a Customer API response, how can an agent tell me whether some downstream consumer still needs it? That question led me to build an API Compatibility Agent around Spring Boot, Flask, Hindsight, and Groq. The interesting part was not teaching the system that removing a field can be breaking. That is easy. The interesting part was giving it memory so it could connect a proposed change to a dependency recorded earlier.

articles.excerpt: Plenty of people keep this as a saved filter in Jira: worklogAuthor = currentUser() AND worklogDate >= startOfWeek() On a Jira Cloud site with Tempo Timesheets it comes back empty for anyone who logs…
articles.body: Plenty of people keep this as a saved filter in Jira: worklogAuthor = currentUser () AND worklogDate >= startOfWeek () On a Jira Cloud site with Tempo Timesheets it comes back empty for anyone who logs time through Tempo, even after a full week of logging, and there's nothing wrong with the query. If you open the Work log tab on any issue, the entries are by "Timesheets by Tempo - Jira Time Tracking" (older sites and screenshots show "Tempo Timesheets"), and each one has "time tracking" as its comment. What Tempo does on Jira Cloud Tempo Cloud keeps worklogs in its own database. When you log time in Tempo, it also creates a worklog in Jira so the issue totals stay right, and that Jira worklog goes under Tempo's own app account.

articles.body: TL;DR The Google Recorder app’s “Allow recordings in other apps” toggle is now rolling out to Pixel users. This toggle is enabled by default, and all your existing audio files will appear in a folder named Recordings in the file manager app of your choice. We first discovered this toggle last week, and it’s already appearing in the latest version of the audio recording app. When it comes to audio recording apps, the Pixel-exclusive Google Recorder covers all the bases. It can automatically transcribe your audio files and cleverly sync them to the cloud for easier access across devices. However, because recordings are sandboxed away from the rest of your storage, file manager apps can’t access them. Fortunately, we knew this could change soon , and that day is finally here.

While the incident doesn't quite rise to the level of the Hugging Face hack , or the recent attacks on US government sites , it's yet another concerning example of AI agents going outside the normal bounds to accomplish a task. According to Howard-Jones, the agents were likely tasked with retrieving publicly available data related to the Productive Capacities Index (PCI) through the UNCTADstat API.
